title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming formatting stability
author: Samira Khan
release_notes: Add OpenAI /v1/chat.completions API parity: support params, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting, and improved streaming stability. Backwards-compatible; config flags for staged rollout.
body: Motivation: Customers expect parity with the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions surface to make migration to Redwood easier and to support existing client tooling (params, roles, stop sequences, logprobs, and structured response formatting). This PR implements the compatibility layer, fixes several streaming edge-cases, and ensures consistent formatted output for both streaming and non-streaming paths. Summary of changes: added full mapping for chat parameters (temperature, top_p, presence_penalty), explicit role handling (system/user/assistant), stop token handling across batching/streaming, opt-in logprobs support (when model exposes it), and response formatter to normalize OpenAI-compatible payloads including truncated/partial tokens in streaming mode. Checklist: - [x] implement parameter mapping and validation - [x] implement roles normalization and tests - [x] implement stop sequence logic for batch + streaming - [x] implement logprobs passthrough with size guardrails - [x] unify streaming and non-streaming formatted output - [x] add unit + integration tests - [x] update docs + examples - [x] staged feature flag and rollout plan Implementation notes: The compatibility layer lives under internal/openai_compat and exposes a single handler that accepts OpenAI-style JSON and translates into internal request objects. Streaming stability fixes: the streamer now flushes partial tokens only when token boundaries are stable, and ensures stop token detection runs against both buffered and incoming token segments to avoid emitting disallowed content. To keep rollout safe the feature is behind the flag OPENAI_COMPAT_CHAT_V1 and gated per-tenant during the initial release. Testing: unit tests cover stop edge-cases (overlapping stop sequences, split-token stops), roles permutation tests, and logprobs size/overflow checks. Integration tests exercise both streaming and non-streaming endpoints against a mocked model backend to validate parity. Backwards compatibility: By default behavior is unchanged; OpenAI-compat is only enabled when the compatibility flag is set or when requests explicitly target /v1/chat.completions. Metrics: added parity-specific tracing and counting (compat.requests, compat.stop_matches, compat.logprobs_dropped). Rollout: enable for internal tenants -> staged customers -> public GA. See linked Linear ENG-4821 for rollout checklist and monitoring dashboards.
commits: feat(openai_compat): add chat.completions handler and request mapping
fix(streaming): stabilize token flush boundaries to avoid partial stop emission
feat(formatter): unified response formatter for streaming + non-streaming OpenAI payloads
test(openai_compat): add unit/integration tests for roles, stop sequences, and logprobs
docs(openai-compat): document /v1/chat.completions mapping and rollout notes
chore: feature flag OPENAI_COMPAT_CHAT_V1 and staged rollout config
review_comments: Ethan Brooks: Left a couple of nits in formatter.py - please prefer explicit JSON schema validation rather than ad-hoc checks.
Samira Khan: Thanks - added jsonschema validation and a small compatibility shim to keep old callers working.
Liu Wei: Streaming fix looks good but please add an integration test that simulates a split stop token across two chunks.
Samira Khan: Added test_chat_stop_sequences.py with the split-token scenario (added mocked token boundary runner).
Nina Patel: Can we gate logprobs behind size checks? risk of huge memory growth in batch responses.
Samira Khan: Added a logprobs_size_limit config and fallback to omit detailed logprobs with a diagnostic counter.
notes_testing: added integration test that validates streamed stop detection and response formatting
benchmarks: streaming throughput fell ~3% in worst-case due to additional stop checks; overall latency improved for short chattings due to better flushing heuristics
